nodes.name: Boston Harbor (Olympia)
nodes.description: A quiet shoal-fringed point at the mouth of Budd Inlet, sheltered from southern gales by tall Douglas firs.

nodes.name: Budd Inlet
nodes.description: A narrow southern reach ending in wide mudflats fed by the Deschutes River, often wrapped in morning mist.

nodes.name: Hope Island
nodes.description: A low, forested island in South Sound rimmed with gravel beaches and calm anchorages.

nodes.name: Anderson Island
nodes.description: The southernmost island of Puget Sound, marked by wooded bluffs, quiet coves, and drifting channel fog.

nodes.name: Tacoma Narrows
nodes.description: A steep-walled strait less than a mile wide where the entire South Sound forces its tide through in swirling eddies.

nodes.name: Blake Island
nodes.description: An uninhabited timbered island off the Kitsap shore with pebble spits and sweeping views of Mount Rainier.

nodes.name: Bainbridge Island
nodes.description: A deeply indented island across from Elliott Bay, offering protected harbors and dense cedar shores.

nodes.name: Whidbey Island
nodes.description: A long, wind-swept island with grassy prairies and high sandy bluffs facing the open fetch of Admiralty Inlet.

nodes.name: Port Townsend
nodes.description: A deep natural harbor at the northeast tip of the Olympic Peninsula where Puget Sound meets the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

nodes.name: Deception Pass
nodes.description: A rocky gorge between Whidbey and Fidalgo Islands where fierce tidal races boil over submerged ledges.

nodes.name: Anacortes
nodes.description: A sheltered northern point on Fidalgo Island looking across Guemes Channel toward the San Juan archipelago.

nodes.name: Friday Harbor
nodes.description: A snug port on the eastern shore of San Juan Island, reached across open channels swept by northern winds.

nodes.name: Bellingham
nodes.description: A broad mainland bay backed by dense timber and the snow-covered peak of Mount Baker to the east.
